 Order

This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail in Cr.No.1/2024 of Hosakote Police Station Bengaluru District, registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 and 417 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned High Court Government Pleader and perused the material on record.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that, on 30.12.2023 at about 2.00 pm, accused No.1-Manjunatha and his family members called the DGF gold company stating that about 715 grams of gold has been pledged by them in CSB Bank and they wish to release the said gold and sell it to the DGF Gold Company and therefore, requested the DGF Gold Company to arrange a sum of Rs.31,30,000/- for releasing the gold.

On 01.01.2024, the officials of the DGF Gold Company namely Abhilash-complainant and Chethan met Manjunath near CSB Gold Company in Hosakote and after verifying the bills and aadhar card, transferred a sum of Rs.31,30,000/- from their Company to CSB Bank account No.035607869715190001 NC: 2024:KHC:6194 belonging to accused No.1.
After the amount was transferred, accused no.1 refused to release the gold.
On the other hand, he secured accused No.2 and both of them threatened the complainant and snatched a sum of Rs.7,000/- from him.

Further, the entire amount was transferred from the account of accused No.1 to the account of accused No.2 and thereby they cheated the complainant etc.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner is innocent and the entire allegations against him are false.

It is contended that the main allegations are against accused No.1 that he and his family members have called the complainant stating that they require a sum of Rs.31,30,000/-for releasing the gold which was pledged with CSB Gold Company so that they can sell the gold to the complainant's company.
He, therefore, contended that the gold was pledged by accused No.1 and it is he who called the complainant and told him to transfer a sum of Rs.31,30,000/-.
It is further submitted that the account of the petitioner has been freezed during investigation.
He submitted that the petitioner is ready and willing to co-operate with the investigation of the case and abide by any NC: 2024:KHC:6194 conditions which may be imposed by the Court.
Hence, sought to allow the petition.

5. The learned High Court Government Pleader contended that the matter is under investigation and the entire amount has been transferred to the account of the present petitioner i.e., accused No.2, who in turn has transferred the amount to different accounts.
He contends that if the petitioner is enlarged on anticipatory bail, he will not co- operate with the investigation.
Accordingly, he has sought to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: It is alleged in the complaint that a sum of Rs.31,30,000/- was transferred by the complainant to the account of accused No.1 as per his request, but he failed to release the gold and sell it to the complainant's Company.
It is further stated that said accused No.1 has transferred the amount to the account of accused No.2 without the knowledge of the complainant.

Investigation conducted so far reveal that the entire amount of Rs.31,30,000/- was transferred to the account of accused No.2 maintained at CSB Gold Company, Kolar Branch and the said accused has immediately transferred NC: 2024:KHC:6194 the amount to his different bank accounts which are maintained at Bank of Maharashtra, Kolar Branch, Bank of Baroda, Kolar Branch etc.
Balance of Rs.26,15,488/-, which was in his main account has been freezed by the police.
7. Prima facie there are material to show that both the accused have connived together and committed the offence with an intention to cheat the complainant.
It is submitted that accused No.1 is arrested and already enlarged on regular bail.
However, the petitioner is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

If the petitioner surrenders before the jurisdictional Court and files necessary application seeking bail, the same shall be considered and disposed of as expeditiously as possible.
8.
With the above observations, the petition is dismissed.
